page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. A local storage capacity of 7559 GB is bundled with the instance, which is also Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-threaded operations, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic execution. The instance achieved top-tier ratings in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations also registered in the top 10% of benchmarks. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU execution and Passmark memory scores falling into the average category.

The server exhibits a clear tradeoff between high compute density and memory capacity. While memory bandwidth is top-tier, the overall memory allocation is restricted to 2.0 GB per vCPU, which may limit memory-bound applications. For LLM inference, the platform achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for medium and large models, but text generation for small models is weak. This instance is suited for compute-intensive workloads, multi-threaded database operations, static web serving, and large-scale data processing that can leverage the substantial local storage.
